title: A fixed 121.54-day Kapteyn wave lowers HIRES error by 14.6 percent after a free inner wave
abstract: We test whether the known outer Kapteyn signal adds to a separate inner-wave fit in public HIRES velocities. A 121.54-day wave fitted to 48 early HARPS nights lowers weighted squared error in 31 HIRES nights by 14.64 percent. HIRES has its own inner wave, mean, and trend. Joint 30-day-bin resampling gives a gain range from -35.40 to +42.25 percent. Instrument, weight, and year-deletion controls retain positive point scores. Nearby periods also transfer. Conditional Gaussian and sign tests give stronger evidence but hold the early template fixed. The joint uncertainty prevents a firm transfer claim. Separate spectra do not make the period selection blind. A stellar signal, a planet with activity, or noise remain possible. A HARPS-only artifact is not excluded. No new planet or unique physical cause is found. Code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes, and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included. External observation tables are excluded. display.caption: Left: joint resampling ranges for the outer-template scale in HIRES. Zero means no contribution; one means the early HARPS scale. Right: conditional Gaussian power for a known 2.25 m/s wave. This power omits template error and unknown correlated noise.
